title: How does the current self-approval interacts with the meta orchestrator?
body:
@sepo-agent /answer 

- Right now our meta orchestrator agent can launch multiple sub issues and prs 
- If self-approve and self-merge is enabled, it will then check approval and then merge the prs. 

Is it the right, expected behavior? Or should it only start self-approval when it finishes implementing all the PRs?

nodes.body:
Current behavior: **yes, this is the expected behavior in the current code**. Self-approval is a **per-PR post-review gate**, not a parent/meta-orchestrator batch gate.

The chain today is:

- `implement` succeeds -> hand off to `review`
- `review` returns `SHIP` -> hand off to `agent-self-approve` when self-approval is enabled
- `agent-self-approve` returns `APPROVED` -> hand off to `agent-self-merge` when self-merge is enabled

That policy is stated in the orchestrator prompt and enforced in runtime code:
- [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5b201e1027e3fc441a3ecbbae98f447cc72d6765/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L24-L34)
- [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5b201e1027e3fc441a3ecbbae98f447cc72d6765/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L461-L511)
- actual workflow dispatch happens in [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5b201e1027e3fc441a3ecbbae98f447cc72d6765/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1543-L1575)

For sub-orchestration, the parent only resumes when the child reaches a terminal result. With self-merge enabled, `agent-self-merge` terminal states like `merged` or `auto_merge_enabled` map to parent child-state `done`, so the parent continues after that PR has reached the self-merge terminal point:
- [`sub-orchestration.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5b201e1027e3fc441a3ecbbae98f447cc72d6765/.agent/src/sub-orchestration.ts#L186-L211)
- [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5b201e1027e3fc441a3ecbbae98f447cc72d6765/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L994-L1071)

So I would summarize it this way:

- For **independent child PRs**, current behavior is reasonable: each PR can be reviewed, self-approved, and merged once it independently passes.
- For **one logical meta task split into stacked or dependent PRs**, I do **not** think global immediate self-merge is the ideal product behavior. In that case, the safer behavior is to defer self-approval/self-merge until the parent orchestrator decides the whole plan is complete, then finalize PRs in dependency order.

I would not change the global default to “wait for all PRs” because single-PR and independent-subtask flows should not be blocked by parent orchestration. The better change is an explicit meta-orchestration policy, for example:

1. Mark child issues/PRs as `independent` vs `batch/stacked`.
2. For `independent`, keep today’s per-PR self-approval/self-merge.
3. For `batch/stacked`, stop after `SHIP` and report “ready” to the parent instead of dispatching `agent-self-approve`.
4. Let the parent orchestrator dispatch final self-approval/self-merge only after it has no more child work, in the correct PR order.

That preserves the current safe PR-level checks while avoiding accidental early merges for multi-PR plans.
@sepo-agent /implement sketch a small PR for this?
